description: Sanitized copies of the ColPali/ViDoRe trial's native outputs, its self-written wrappers, and the self-contained CPU reproduction run. Log timestamps inside files are host local time (UTC-4) unless marked Z.
sanitization_policy: Private originals are not published; their name, byte count and sha256 are recorded here. They were in this session's scratch directory: the first pass's trees, which the first polish pass deleted on 2026-09-26 at 06:39Z (../host-cleanup-20260926/first-pass-scratch-trees/), or the port's and polish passes' own trees (trials-2, trials-pol), which remain (../README.md#host-state). Published copies replace the session scratch path with <scratch>, the home directory with ~, the user name with <user> (also inside underscore-encoded paths), UUID-shaped identifiers with <uuid>, and credential values with <redacted>; excerpts mark every omitted line range in place. Files marked verbatim are byte-for-byte copies. Each published copy passed scripts/validate.py PRIVATE_CONTENT and a credential-shape check.

First pass, full 280-row split on CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' in local-integration/run_eval_colpali.sh, whose set -x trace opens this log). Queries finished (7 pre-batches, 5 min 20 s); the CLI then embeds all 280 row images (7 pre-batches x 10 batches of 4). The first 6 of those 70 image batches finished at elapsed 2:42, 5:59, 9:47, 13:24, 17:11 and 21:14 of the document pass: 162, 197, 228, 217, 227 and 243 s per batch. tqdm's s/it column (162.54 to 224.56) is its smoothed rate (a bias-corrected moving average with smoothing 0.3, which these per-batch times reproduce), not a per-batch time. The log then stops without an EVAL_EXIT line, a bash `time` summary or metrics. How the process ended was not retained: the first pass reported a 1700 s timeout, but neither the script nor this log shows one.

outputs.what: Diagnostic probe for the colqwen2 processor TypeError of attempts 5 and 6 (polish pass). It calls transformers' list_repo_templates and colpali-engine's ColQwen2Processor / ColQwen2_5_Processor.from_pretrained directly, with every step's expected outcome written in the file before the run. Our driver around upstream functions, not an upstream test; it downloads processor and tokenizer files only, never model weights.

Output (one JSON object per line) of local-integration/colqwen_processor_probe.py, 2026-09-26T06:34:23Z-06:34:37Z, CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''), fresh private HF_HOME and HOME, no Hub token, in the first pass's .venv-combined, whose installed set equalled reproduction/requirements-lock.txt (the same 94 pins; transformers 4.53.1, huggingface_hub 0.36.2, colpali-engine 0.3.13, vidore-benchmark 5.0.0, torch 2.8.0). Self-contained CPU reproduction: fresh mktemp venv installed from requirements-lock.txt with the installed set checked equal to it, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' checked through torch, pinned Hub revisions into a private HF_HOME, the slice rebuilt and checked byte-identical, then the unchanged evaluate-retriever CLI for colpali and for the dummy control under /usr/bin/time -v, and removal of the workspace. run-20260926T0412Z executed this exact version (the file is older than the run and unchanged since). Our glue around the upstream CLI.

Slice builder used by reproduce-cpu.sh: loads the test split of the pinned vidore/tabfquad_test_subsampled snapshot, keeps its first 12 rows, writes them with the datasets library's to_parquet, and compares per-row query and image sha256 with slice-expected.json (exit 0 only on a match); our glue.
Fingerprint of the first pass's 12-row input (per-row query and image sha256 and the parquet sha256; hashes only) that build_slice.py compares the rebuilt slice with; input to our check.
